genesis.21.p1.b1.text: Now the LORD attended to Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah what He had promised.

genesis.21.p1.b2.text: So Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the very time God had promised.

genesis.21.p1.b3.text: And Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore to him.

genesis.21.p1.b4.text: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

genesis.21.p2.b5.text: God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me.

genesis.21.p2.b6.text: Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have borne him a son in his old age.

genesis.21.p2.b7.text: So the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.

genesis.21.p3.b8.text: But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking her son,

genesis.21.p3.b9.text: Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac!

genesis.21.p3.b10.text: Now this matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son Ishmael.

genesis.21.p3.b11.text: Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant. … for through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.

genesis.21.p3.b12.text: But I will also make a nation of the slave woman’s son, because he is your offspring.”

genesis.21.p4.b13.text: Early in the morning, Abraham got up, took bread and a skin of water, put them on Hagar’s shoulders, and sent her away with the boy.

genesis.21.p4.b14.text: She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.

genesis.21.p5.b15.text: When the water in the skin was gone, she left the boy under one of the bushes.

genesis.21.p5.b16.text: Then she went off and sat down nearby, about a bowshot away,

genesis.21.p5.b17.text: I cannot bear to watch the boy die!

genesis.21.p5.b18.text: And as she sat nearby, she lifted up her voice and wept.

genesis.21.p6.b19.text: Then God heard the voice of the boy, and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven,

genesis.21.p6.b20.text: What is wrong, Hagar? Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies.

genesis.21.p6.b21.text: Get up, lift up the boy, and take him by the hand, for I will make him into a great nation.”

genesis.21.p6.b22.text: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water.

genesis.21.p6.b23.text: So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink.

genesis.21.p7.b24.text: And God was with the boy, and he grew up and settled in the wilderness and became a great archer.

genesis.21.p7.b25.text: And while he was dwelling in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother got a wife for him from the land of Egypt.

genesis.21.p7.b26.text: God is with you in all that you do. Now, therefore, swear to me here before God …

genesis.21.p8.b28.text: But when Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well that Abimelech’s servants had seized,

genesis.21.p8.b29.text: I do not know who has done this. You did not tell me, so I have not heard about it until today.

genesis.21.p8.b30.text: You are to accept the seven ewe lambs from my hand as my witness that I dug this well.

genesis.21.p8.b31.text: So that place was called Beersheba, because it was there that the two of them swore an oath.

genesis.21.p8.b32.text: And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba, and there he called upon the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.
